title: US midterm elections 2026: What do upcoming elections in the US mean for Sensex, Nifty 50? Experts weigh in | Stock Market News
text:
US midterm elections 2026: The US midterm elections are scheduled for November 3, 2026, and are expected to keep global financial markets on edge, with the outcome likely to influence investor sentiment, US economic policies and cross-border capital flows.

For Indian stock market, the elections come at a time when investors are closely monitoring foreign institutional investor (FII) activity, the rupee's movement against the US dollar, crude oil prices and US Treasury bond yields.

The elections will determine which political party controls the two chambers of the US Congress — the House of Representatives and the Senate — for the next two years. All 435 seats in the House and roughly one-third of the Senate seats are up for election. Depending on the outcome, President Donald Trump's ability to push forward his tax, spending and regulatory agenda could face fewer or more legislative hurdles.

For Indian investors, the key question is how the election outcome could influence global liquidity, foreign investment flows and sector-specific opportunities.

Market analysts believe that while the results could trigger short-term volatility in the Sensex and Nifty 50, the broader market direction will depend on several other factors, including geopolitical developments, crude oil prices, interest-rate expectations and corporate earnings.

Sugandha Sachdeva, Founder of SS WealthStreet, outlined three possible scenarios and their potential implications for global markets and Indian equities.

A divided Congress could limit Trump's ability to implement his tax and spending plans, increasing the possibility of legislative gridlock and government shutdowns. However, a check on fiscal expansion could ease US bond yields and dollar strength, potentially offering support to the Indian rupee and helping moderate FII outflows from domestic equities.

If Republicans retain both the House and Senate, the Trump administration could have greater flexibility to pursue tax cuts and higher government spending. This could support US equities, but an expansion in fiscal deficits may keep Treasury yields and the dollar elevated. Such a trend could put pressure on emerging markets, including India, through foreign capital outflows and currency weakness.

A Democratic majority in both chambers could create significant resistance to Trump's legislative agenda. Greater scrutiny of artificial intelligence (AI) and technology companies could also weigh on US technology stocks, potentially affecting Indian IT stocks and broader market sentiment. However, a more restrained fiscal approach could eventually support emerging markets by easing concerns around US borrowing and bond yields.

According to Seema Srivastava, Senior Research Analyst at SMC Global Securities, the US midterm elections could influence Indian equities through changes in US economic policies, trade tariffs, geopolitical relations, interest-rate expectations and global investor sentiment.

She said the impact on Indian markets would largely be transmitted through FII flows, the US dollar, Treasury yields and crude oil prices. A stronger dollar and rising US 10-year Treasury yields could make American assets more attractive, encouraging foreign investors to shift capital away from emerging markets such as India. Conversely, easing bond yields and a weaker dollar could improve global liquidity and support foreign investment in domestic equities.

Historically, Indian equities have delivered positive returns in several periods following US midterm elections, although the performance has not been consistent. According to Srivastava, investors should view the election as a potential source of short-term volatility rather than an independent trigger for a sustained market rally or correction.

Recent market analysis has also highlighted that Indian equities do not necessarily replicate Wall Street's post-election performance. Domestic earnings growth, valuations and foreign capital flows remain important determinants of market returns.
